Admin.title: Admin
Admin.description: Represents an administrator user with elevated privileges.

uid.description: The unique identifier of the user who is an admin. This matches the user's ID in Firebase Authentication.

assignedAt.description: The timestamp when the user was made an admin.

User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the application.

uid.description: Unique identifier for the user, matching Firebase Auth UID.

photoURL.description: URL of the user's profile picture.

isAdmin.description: Flag indicating if the user has administrative privileges.

disabled.description: Flag indicating if the user's account is disabled.

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the user account was created.

lastLoginAt.description: The timestamp of the user's last login.

autoDisablePolicy.description: Policy for automatically disabling the user account.

CeilingProject.title: CeilingProject
CeilingProject.description: Represents a ceiling project with its dimensions and visual aspects.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CeilingProject entity.

projectName.description: The user-defined name for the ceiling project.

length.description: The length measurement of the ceiling.

width.description: The width measurement of the ceiling.

numberOfSections.description: The number of equal sections the ceiling is divided into.

textureImageUri.description: URI of the texture image applied to the ceiling drawing.

drawingData.description: Data representing the generated 2D drawing of the ceiling layout.

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the project was created.

HomeScreenImage.title: HomeScreenImage
HomeScreenImage.description: Represents the image displayed on the home screen of the application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the HomeScreenImage entity.

imageUri.description: URI of the beautifully finished ceiling image.

description.description: A brief description of the image.

isActive.description: Indicates whether this image is currently active and displayed on the home screen.

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore structure now includes a top-level `users` collection for public profiles and an `admins` collection to manage privileges. This is more scalable and secure. The `admins` collection uses Document ID as UID for fast, cost-effective security checks (`exists()`). User-specific data (`ceilingProjects`) remains nested under the user's document, maintaining Path-Based Ownership for privacy. Admins are granted broad access to manage users and content.
